message.reasoning_content: Claims c1 and c2 already cover the main risks. Any additional testable in-scope claims? One more: trailing pivot could be nonpositive/near zero due to rank-7 Gram + 2^-10 regularizer — the last pivot in exact arithmetic is det ratio; since factor is 8x7, A = F F^T + eps I has rank 7 + eps, so eigenvalue 8 is ~eps. Exact pivots: the 8th pivot of no-pivot elimination equals something small ~2^-10. log(p7) ≈ log(2^-10) ≈ -6.9. That's fine but elimination float32 error on trailing pivot of magnitude ~1e-3 relative to entries ~100 could be catastrophic: absolute error ~1e-3*ulp(~100)... Actually cancellation in updated = matrix - product where matrix entries ~O(100) and product ~O(100), the difference ~1e-3 — float32 relative error gives absolute error ~100*6e-8=6e-6, relative to pivot 1e-3 that's ~0.6% error in the last pivot → log error ~6e-3, exceeding 1e-4. This is really a sub-mechanism of c1 but worth a distinct claim about the last pivot being at the regularizer scale. But c1 already covers it. The claims are fine; the key question is whether elimination without pivoting even on the exact matrix has pivots collapsing. That's part of c1's rationale. I think no new claims; record_no_new_claims.
